text:
linda: hitting a weird install/import issue with the Python SDK when using poetry editable on macOS M1. after `poetry install -E async` I get `ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood'`

alex: can you paste the install steps + python/pip versions?

linda: sure —
```
python -V
# Python 3.11.4
poetry --version
# Poetry 1.5.1
poetry add --editable ../redwood-sdk[async]  # local dev install
# then in REPL: from redwood import AsyncClient  -> ImportError
```

sam: editable installs with PEP 517 backends sometimes don't expose package data (py.typed) or exported names until build-backend glues things. do you see the package installed as an egg-link or a wheel? `pip show redwood`

linda: pip show redwood ->
```
Name: redwood
Version: 0.4.1
Location: /Users/linda/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/app-py3.11/lib/python3.11/site-packages
Files: __init__.py, client.py, ...
```
but `dir(redwood)` doesn't show AsyncClient. looks like the top-level package `redwood` exports Client only. in src/redwood/__init__.py we had: `from .client import Client` but AsyncClient is in `async_client.py` and not imported in __init__ in the wheel build. works when i do `pip install -e .` but not with poetry editable.

alex: ok that explains the import error. Two problems to fix in the repo:
- export AsyncClient from package root if we want `from redwood import AsyncClient`
- include `py.typed` so typing users get stubs (PEP 561)

sara: also check wheel tags for mac + M1. CI produced only manylinux wheels, no macosx universal2 wheel — that can bite local devs using binary dependencies. but your import issue is purely about exports.

linda: i can hack a quick `from .async_client import AsyncClient` into __init__.py locally and it works. curious why `poetry install -E async` didn't pick that up while `pip install -e .` did — both should use the same source.

sam: poetry editable uses a different install path (`.pth` vs symlink) historically, and if build-backend uses package_dir or dynamic exports it can differ. Also if your packaging uses `exports = find:` in pyproject but you have a MANIFEST.in mismatch, the built sdist/wheel may lack files.

linda: any quick fix we can push so other devs don't hit this in their first-time setup? onboarding hit: new hires hit this and think the SDK is broken.

alex: propose we do a patch release 0.4.2 with these three changes:
1) add `from .async_client import AsyncClient` to src/redwood/__init__.py
2) include `py.typed` and ensure `package_data`/`include` in pyproject: `include = ["redwood/py.typed"]`
3) adjust CI to build and publish macos universal2 wheels (set up `cibuildwheel` with `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` + `pyproject` metadata)

linda: that would be great. also while we're at it, add a small note in README about editable installs with Poetry (rare pitfalls) and a `dev-setup.md` for local testing.

sara: +1. i can add the cibuildwheel job and test publish to our test pypi. will ping when a test wheel is up.

ci-bot: CI pipeline update: release/0.4.2 branch created by alex — failing macos wheel job (archives missing), see logs https://ci.internal.redwood/reports/1820001234 (log excerpt: `ERROR: no matching wheel for platform macosx_11_0_universal2`)

alex: thanks bot — will iterate. also adding typing: we should enable `py.typed` and run `mypy --config-file` in CI to catch missing exports.

sam: FYI for maintainers: if you prefer not to export AsyncClient at package root, add to docs that async client import path is `from redwood.async_client import AsyncClient`. but most users expect parity between sync/async imports.

linda: noted. once 0.4.2 is out i'll retest the onboarding script. thanks folks :)

sara: created test wheels on testpypi, 0.4.2rc1 includes exports + py.typed and macos universal2. @linda can you try `pip install -i https://test.pypi.org/simple redwood==0.4.2rc1` and confirm?

linda: installing now... `pip install -i https://test.pypi.org/simple redwood==0.4.2rc1` -> works, `from redwood import AsyncClient` succeeds and mypy sees types. marking as resolved for onboarding until final release. :tada:
